evals.prompt: Turn the research brief into a PRD for the task-priorities feature.
evals.expected_output: A prd.md (frontmatter goals/non_goals/metrics/acceptance) with user stories, traceable to the research brief, under docs/sdlc/<feature>/. No technical design or code.
assertions: A prd.md handoff is produced with frontmatter listing goals and acceptance criteria
Non-goals and success metrics are stated
User stories are written for the change
The requirements trace back to the research brief's findings/recommendation
Only product requirements are produced — no technical design or code

evals.prompt: Define the goals, non-goals, and acceptance criteria for the new feature.
evals.expected_output: A product spec stating goals, non-goals, metrics, and testable acceptance criteria.
assertions: Goals and explicit non-goals are stated
Acceptance criteria are concrete and testable
The output is a product spec, not an architecture or a task plan

evals.prompt: Write the user stories and acceptance criteria for task priorities.
evals.expected_output: User stories with acceptance criteria mapping to the feature's goals.
assertions: User stories are written from the user's perspective
The stories cover the feature's goals

component.purpose: Phase workflow: turn a research-brief into product requirements — assess the current product, define goals/non-goals/metrics/acceptance and user stories, and produce a prd.md handoff. Gated at Tier-1 (routing); quality via the prd schema + traceability to the brief.

should_trigger: Write a PRD for the task-priorities feature
Define the goals and acceptance criteria for the new feature
Turn the research brief into a product spec
Specify the requirements and user stories for X
Produce the product requirements for the feature
should_not_trigger: Research the options and prior art for X before we spec it
Design the technical architecture for the feature
Break the design into a dependency-ordered task plan
Implement the feature in a worktree
